newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - China, HK and Taiwan deals.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - China, HK and Taiwan deals.

text.p: News of upcoming deals for Taiwan, Hong Kong and Chinese entities enlivened a slow Asian debt markets session on Wednesday.
Bankers said Union Bank of Taiwan has mandated WestLB, Societe Generale Asia and First Chicago Bank to arrange a US$50 million floating rate certificate of deposit issue.
The facility has a final maturity of three years with a put option in year two, they said.
Price talk is around 32 basis points over the London Interbank Offered Rate and syndication will start next week.

Last April, Union Bank set a three-year FRCD with annual puts and calls that paid an all-in of 38 basis points. The issue was increased to US$50 million from US$30 million because of oversubscription in syndication.
Bankers said government-owned Land Bank of Taiwan is considering a US$100 million FRCD with a final maturity of three or five years.
Sources close to the transaction said the issuer's funding requirements are not urgent and that it might withdraw the issue "if pricing is not satisfactory."
Bankers said they suspect that Land Bank will be looking for pricing similar to that achieved by state-owned Bank of Taiwan.
Bank of Taiwan launched a five-year US$200 million floating rate note last November that paid an all-in return of 11 basis points over LIBOR.
Bankers said that kind of spread might be too tight to entice many lenders to Land Bank.
Because Land Bank is not a commercial bank, participating in the deal would not offer any promise of future business, one banker said.
But some lenders might be keen to develop a positive relationship with the Taiwan government by lending to a state-held institution, he acknowledged.

In Hong Kong, bankers say that Hysan Development is pondering a HK$2 billion floating rate note issue, proceeds of which could be used to finance its recent acquisition of a prime property in the heart of the territory's central district.
The issue would probably have a tenor of five years, they said.
Such an issue would be Hysan's first FRN and a rare capital markets issue for a Hong Kong property developer. Pricing might be difficult, some bankers said.
Hong Kong's property companies are big borrowers but tend to prefer the loan market. Hysan has borrowed via loans and with covertible bonds in the past.
In news of China, bankers said that China Merchant Bank and China Construction Bank are mulling new issues.

Meanwhile, a Yankee bond for State Development Bank of China, which was mandated to J.P. Morgan and Lehman Brothers months ago, now looks closer to launch. Talk of a bond issue for Bank of China also continues to circulate.
Elsewhere, officials from Argentina were in Hong Kong Wednesday roadshowing the republic's upcoming US$2.0 billion global bond. Merrill Lynch and J.P. Morgan are joint leads.
Some 50 to 80 potential investors attended each of three Asian roadshows, which were held in Seoul, Taipei and Hong Kong, the officials said.
